topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and sources of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations accumulate and confer clonal advantages under conditions that permit cancer development.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and uncertainty surrounding how environmental exposure contributes to cancer rather than cancer being simply inevitable or random.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the interaction between pathogens and cellular changes.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage through processes whose effects depend on metabolism and the exposed tissue.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutagenic initiation may require a subsequent growth-promoting environment for tumours to develop.

topics.label: Developmental susceptibility and recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the mechanistic account by explaining developmental susceptibility and then summarising how carcinogenic effects depend on biological context.

topics.label: Investigating carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence of carcinogenicity can be obtained and why the available approaches cannot fully establish cancer causation on their own.

topics.label: Concluding summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by consolidating its conclusions and placing everyday exposure decisions in a risk–benefit framework.
